survivors.claim: The spec plugin's 7.291.0 changelog paragraph claims the mocks driver's dispatch lines print the policy.models seats, but the diff changes no dispatch line in mocks-driver.js (D7 names only the build and review drivers) and the file contains no `model:` dispatch line at all.
survivors.impact: The released changelog describes a behaviour the plugin does not have, so a host reading it will expect the wireframe driver to honour a model override that never reaches it.
survivors.evidence: plugin.json:39 text: '…and the build/review/mocks driver dispatch lines print the policy.models seats.' Executed: grep -n "model:" spec/scripts/mocks-driver.js → no output; the range diff of spec/scripts/mocks-driver.js touches only the import line and the connect-hint gate (D6).

survivors.claim: Three remedy-text dispatch lines in the review driver still print a bare Agent {subagent_type: "spec:reviewer"} / Agent {subagent_type: "spec:disposer"} with no model/effort, while the Goal says every driver dispatch line prints the seat from policy.models. D7 enumerates only the REVIEWER, DISPOSITIONS and ESCALATE sites, so this is bent intent, not a contradiction.
survivors.impact: A session that follows a re-dispatch remedy after a failed reviewer or missing disposer return will spawn the agent on its file-frontmatter seat, bypassing the host's override at exactly the retry where it was already applied once.
survivors.evidence: Executed grep -n subagent_type spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js: lines 1323, 1474, 1489 carry no seatArgs(); lines 2598/2607/2641/2679 do. Spec Goal: 'every driver dispatch line prints the model and effort policy.models names for that seat'.

survivors.claim: stage-review.md's fix-worker bullet still hard-codes the fix seat as sonnet at effort: medium while the review driver's fix-dispatch sentence (same step) now reads policy.models.workers — doctrine and driver now disagree on a host with a workers override.
survivors.impact: On a host that overrides the worker seat, the printed step and the doctrine the session is grounded on name two different models for the same fix dispatch.
survivors.evidence: stage-review.md:60: 'dispatches a worker (`sonnet` at `effort: medium`, core § Model Placement; via `agentMap`)'. spec-review-driver.js:2563 reads policy(repoRoot).models.workers. D7 directs the stage-review edit only for the reviewer and disposer bullets, so this is drift, not a spec violation.

survivors.claim: Six near-identical 'read spec.config.json → cfg.policy = block → write back' blocks across four test files in this diff; the rules' duplication calibration names the extraction — a setPolicy(root, block) helper in tests/helpers.js.
survivors.impact: The next spec that adds a policy reader copies a seventh block, and any change to where the config lives has six places to miss.
